To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

protein incorporation by isolated oocytes is mediated by a micropinocytic process, that the rate of protein uptake is constant over time and is not dependent upon the amount of protein added, that the rate is sensitive to the temperature of the medium and its ionic composition, and that the optimal conditions for protein uptake are a temperature of 18-20 degrees C and a medium of pH 7.4 containing 0.2 M NaCl, 0.01 M KCl,

protein incorporation by oocytes is a process of microropinocytosis that is sensitive to temperature and ionic composition, and that the standard medium can be improved by the addition of calcium and magnesium.

protein uptake by amphibian oocyte is a process of microrpinocytosis that is temperature sensitive and dependent on the ionic composition, especially calcium, of the medium in which the oocytes are incubated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the uptake of exogenous macromolecules by isolated oocytes.
the study of protein incorporation by amphibians oocytes.
the mechanism of protein incorporation by isolated oocytes and its possible application to the study of the synthesis of specific proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the standard medium is the best one for protein incorporation by amphibia oocytes.

the standard incubation conditions for the incorporation of protein into amphibian oocytes are: 0.5 M NaCl; 0.01 M KCl; 0 1 mM MgCl2; 0.1 M CaCl2; 10 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.5) and 0.1% bovine serum albumin.
the optimum medium for protein incorporation by amphibia oocytes is a solution of 0.1 M NaCl, 0.02 M KCl, and 0.02 mM CaCl2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
protein incorporation by isolated oocytes is a highly sensitive and reproducible system for investigating the process of pinocytosis.
oocytes are capable of incorporating proteins in vitro under a variety of conditions and that the optimum conditions are those which most closely approximate the in situ environment.

protein incorporation is most efficiently accomplished by incubating oocytes at 20 degrees in a medium consisting of 0.5% bovine serum albumin, 10 mM sodium pyruvate, 10 mM Tris, 0.1 mM CaCl2, and 0.1 M NaCl, pH 7.6.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein uptake by oocytes is a highly sensitive process that can be used to study protein-protein interactions, protein-ligand interactions, and the effects of protein structure on protein function.
the standard incubation conditions we have used for over 40 years are still valid, but that the conditions can be modified to optimize the incorporation of specific proteins.
the standard medium is a good starting point and that the conditions can be adjusted to suit the particular requirements of the investigator.
